title: Fantasy Player News
description: Breaking Fantasy Football player news along with the impact for fantasy managers

items.author: Garrett Ball
items.title: Baltimore Ravens D/ST struggle against Jacksonville
items.desc: The Baltimore Ravens D/ST was run over by the Jaguars on Thursday, allowing 33 points in the 23-point loss. They did manage a fumble recovery, but that was the only real counting stat they managed.
items.impact: It was a rough showing by the Ravens' unit, but they weren't helped by the offense, which often gave the Jaguars short fields to work with, putting more pressure on the defense. They will look to get things back on track against the Chargers.

items.author: Garrett Ball
items.title: Jake Moody hits four kicking points in loss
items.desc: Jake Moody hit his only field goal and PAT attempts in the Ravens' 33-10 loss to Jacksonville on Thursday,
items.impact: Moody filled in well for the injured Tyler Loop, but didn't get much of a chance to put points on the board. Hopefully things will improve for the Ravens in the coming weeks.

items.author: Garrett Ball
items.title: Justice Hill breaks away for long TD in loss
items.desc: Justice Hill ran nine times for 85 yards and a touchdown in the Ravens' 33-10 loss to the Jaguars on Thursday. He also caught three passes for seven yards.
items.impact: Hill managed the one explosive play by the Ravens all night, breaking away for a long touchdown late in the game. He could be an interesting flex option moving forward as the Ravens change of pace back.

items.author: Garrett Ball
items.title: Ja'Kobi Lane held without a catch in loss
items.desc: Ja'Kobi Lane was held without a catch in the Ravens' 33-10 loss to the Jaguars on Thursday.
items.impact: Lane has only one catch in the last two games, but it's hard to take away much from Thursday's game, where the Ravens only had 10 completions, and their leading receiver had only 19 yards. So don't lose hope on Lane just yet.

items.author: Garrett Ball
items.title: Rashod Bateman hauls in short pass in loss
items.desc: Rashod Bateman caught one of two targets for six yards in the Ravens' 33-10 loss to the Jaguars on Thursday.
items.impact: Bateman has two catches in as many weeks, and he's fallen out of relevance for fantasy. Leave him on waivers until he shows some sort of value.

items.author: Garrett Ball
items.title: Mark Andrews snags two passes in loss
items.desc: Mark Andrews caught both of his targets for 19 yards in the Ravens' 33-10 loss to the Jaguars on Thursday.
items.impact: Andrews led the Ravens in receiving yards in the blowout loss, not that it meant much for fantasy. He's been tough to trust at any point this season and is safe to leave on the waiver wire. However, if you want to hold on and see what he might do with Jacoby Brissett at QB, there's merit to that.

items.author: Garrett Ball
items.title: Zay Flowers manages 23 yards in loss to Jags
items.desc: Zay Flowers caught three of six targets for 6 yards and ran three times for 17 yards in the Ravens' 33-10 loss to the Jaguars on Thursday.
items.impact: Flowers had three more catches than he had on Sunday, but it didn't amount to much. Jacoby Brissett should bring back some life to the fantasy value of Flowers once he takes the reins of the offense, and thankfully that should come next week.

items.author: Garrett Ball
items.title: Joe Fagnano struggles in spot start on TNF
items.desc: Joe Fagnano completed 10 of 18 passes for 60 yards with two interceptions in the Ravens' 33-10 loss to the Jaguars. He also ran three times for 13 yards.
items.impact: Fagnano's first NFL start actually got off decently well; he showed confidence and was rushing to get first downs. However, that eroded quickly as the Jaguars figured things out, and he had no answers. The Ravens' finalized their trade for Jacoby Brissett on Friday, so this will likely be Fagnano's only start unless Brissett also suffers an injury.

items.author: Garrett Ball
items.title: Derrick Henry struggles in loss to Jaguars
items.desc: Derrick Henry ran 17 times for 57 yards in the Ravens' 33-10 loss to the Jaguars on Thursday.
items.impact: Henry didn't have a touchdown or a reception to save his lackluster rushing totals, as the Jaguars bottled him up all night. The Ravens have now scored no more than 13 points in each of the last four games, and Henry's fantasy points are evidence of that. He at least gets a favorable matchup against the Chargers next time out.

items.author: Garrett Ball
items.title: Cam Little racks up 15 kicking points in win
items.desc: Cam Little hit all four of his field goal attempts and all three PATs in the Jaguars' 33-10 win over the Ravens.
items.impact: Little now has totals of 10, 7, 7, 6, and 15 kicking points in his last five games. He's been a great play for fantasy and one of the better kickers so far in 2026.

items.author: Garrett Ball
items.title: Jacksonville Jaguars handle Ravens in TNF win
items.desc: The Jacksonville Jaguars D/ST had a sack, a fumble recovery and two interceptions in the Jags' 33-10 win over the Ravens on Thursday.
items.impact: The Jags' defense dominated in this game, granted it didn't hurt that they were facing a third-string quarterback making his first NFL start on a short week. They held the Ravens to a measly 55 passing yards (counting sacks), and routinely messed up the Baltimore run game. They face off next against Tennessee.

items.author: Garrett Ball
items.title: Nate Boerkircher goes for 61 yards in win
items.desc: Nate Boerkircher caught two of three targets for 61 yards in the Jaguars' 33-10 win over the Ravens on Thursday.
items.impact: Boerkircher now has either 61 yards or a touchdown in his last three games on just two targets a game. It's an interesting development for the likes of Brenton Strange, who saw his workload decrease on Thursday night. However, that could just be circumstantial and not prescriptive.

items.author: Garrett Ball
items.title: Brenton Strange goes for 22 yards in win
items.desc: Brenton Strange caught both of his targets for 22 yards in the Jaguars' 33-10 win over the Ravens.
items.impact: It was a bit of a letdown after Strange had been successful in the last few weeks as a streaming tight end play. Nate Boerkircher has started to get more involved in recent weeks, and that could be limiting Strange's upside.

items.author: Garrett Ball
items.title: Brian Thomas Jr. held without a target in win
items.desc: Brian Thomas Jr. was not targeted in the Jaguars' 33-10 win over the Ravens.
items.impact: Thomas caught a touchdown on Sunday, and was held without a target on Thursday. The "downfield threat," as the Jaguars coaching staff has called him, has only 117 yards all season and can be safely dropped, unless you want to hold and hope he gets traded before the deadline.

items.author: Garrett Ball
items.title: Jakobi Meyers snags four passes in win
items.desc: Jakobi Meyers caught four of six passes for 65 yards in the Jaguars' 33-10 win over the Ravens on Thursday.
items.impact: Meyers led the team in receptions and yards, while coming in second in targets. It was the veteran's second-best yardage total of the season, and he now has 65 yards or more in two of his last three games.

items.author: Garrett Ball
items.title: Chris Rodriguez Jr. hammers in touchdown in win over Ravens
items.desc: Chris Rodriguez Jr. ran 10 times fo 19 yards and a touchdown in the Jaguars' 33-10 win over the Ravens. He also caught both of his targets for 13 yards.
items.impact: Rodriguez matched Bhayshul Tuten for touches, but crucially got the receiving work, giving him the edge in half- and full-PPR formats. He's heavily touchdown-dependent, but the good news is he could see another chance to score against the Titans next week if the Jags can build up a big lead.

items.author: Garrett Ball
items.title: Parker Washington snags touchdown in win over Ravens
items.desc: Parker Washington caught two of seven targets for 61 yards and a score in the Jaguars' 33-10 win over the Ravens on Thursday.
items.impact: Almost all of Washington's fantasy points came on a long 50-yard catch-and-run touchdown in the first half. He failed to bring in anything else after that and suffered some drops as well. It wasn't the greatest game for the talented WR, but it certainly could have been much worse.

items.author: Chris Schommer
items.title: Christian McCaffrey (hamstring) off injury report for Week 9
items.desc: Christian McCaffrey (hamstring) is off of the injury report for Week 9 for the San Francisco 49ers according to Nick Wagoner.
items.impact: McCaffrey is good to go once again while fighting through a lingering hamstring issue for head coach Kyle Shanahan, lining up the dynamic running back for another sizeable workload against a generous Raiders defense Sunday.

items.author: Garrett Ball
items.title: Bhayshul Tuten struggles in rainy game
items.desc: Bhayshul Tuten ran 12 times for 29 yards and a touchdown in the Jaguars' 33-10 win over the Ravens on Thursday.
items.impact: Tuten struggled to get much going in this game, with his longest run being six yards. The Ravens' defense did a good job keeping things in front of them and not allowing many explosive plays by the Jags, and Tuten suffered for it. He will look to have a better time out against the Titans next week.

items.author: Garrett Ball
items.title: Trevor Lawrence throws for 242 yards in rainy TNF
items.desc: Trevor Lawrence completed 16 of 26 passes for 242 yards and a touchdown in the Jaguars' 33-10 win over the Ravens. He also ran once for -1 yard.
items.impact: Lawrence didn't have to do much to get his team the win in this game, much like Sunday when he faced the Colts. His one touchdown came on a breakaway play by Parker Washington, who was quiet aside from that play. Lawrence gets another easy matchup next week against the Titans. They will be well rested, however, as Tennessee is on a bye, but the Jaguars have a mini-bye themselves thanks to the Thursday game.

items.author: Chris Schommer
items.title: Mike Evans (achilles) ruled out for Week 9
items.desc: Mike Evans (achilles) has been ruled out for Week 9 for the San Francisco 49ers according to Nick Wagoner.
items.impact: Evans will not suit up after struggling to reach the practice field this week, lining up Demarcus Robinson (ankle) and Brandin Cooks to lead a shorthanded wideout group against the Raiders for head coach Kyle Shanahan Sunday.

items.author: Chris Schommer
items.title: Deebo Samuel Sr. (hamstring) ruled out for Week 9
items.desc: Deebo Samuel Sr. (hamstring) has been ruled out for Week 9 for the San Francisco 49ers according to Nick Wagoner.
items.impact: Samuel Sr. will sit out once again for head coach Kyle Shanahan with an eye towards returning in Week 10, with Brandin Cooks and Demarcus Robinson (ankle) in line to lead a banged-up wideout group against the Raiders Sunday.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Charlie Jones (hand) considered questionable for Sunday
items.desc: Charlie Jones (hand) is considered questionable for Sunday's game against the Philadelphia Eagles.
items.impact: Jones is going to be questionable to play on Sunday. He's managing a hand injury right now, although it doesn't seem to be very serious. His potential absence wouldn't have much of an effect for fantasy purposes.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Cam Skattebo (hamstring) doubtful to play Sunday
items.desc: Cam Skattebo (hamstring) is doubtful to play in Sunday's game against the Philadelphia Eagles.
items.impact: Skattebo wasn't able to practice on Friday and is officially considered doubtful to play heading into the weekend. It remains to be seen if he will miss more time beyond this game due to his hamstring issue, and fantasy managers should expect Devin Singletary to serve as the team's clear-cut RB1 in his absence.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Uchenna Nwosu (ankle) remains out for Sunday
items.desc: Uchenna Nwosu (ankle) will remain out for Sunday's game against the Arizona Cardinals.
items.impact: Nwosu is going to be sidelined for a second-straight game as he continues to recover from an ankle issue of some kind. His next chance to play will come in a matchup against the Raiders next week.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Drew Lock (elbow) good to go for Sunday
items.desc: Drew Lock (elbow) is good to go for Sunday's game against the Arizona Cardinals.
items.impact: As expected, Lock's elbow injury is nothing serious and he is good to go for Sunday's game against Arizona. He is set to be the team's starting quarterback with Sam Darnold (quad/ribs) ruled out, so Jaxon Smith-Njigba projects to be the only viable pass catcher for the Seahawks this week.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Quenton Nelson (knee) considered week-to-week
items.desc: Quenton Nelson (knee) underwent a procedure on his knee and is now considered week-to-week.
items.impact: Nelson underwent a minor surgery on his knee and is going to miss some time while he recovers. He has already been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Cardinals, and he is reportedly considered week-to-week for right now, though he's not expected to land on injured reserve. His absence will be bad news for Seattle's offensive front for the next few weeks, especially with Charles Cross (ankle) also injured right now.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Charles Cross (ankle) unavailable for Sunday
items.desc: Charles Cross (ankle) will be unavailable for Sunday's game against the Arizona Cardinals.
items.impact: To no surprise, Cross is going to be sidelined for another game on Sunday. Seattle's offensive front is set to be much weaker than usual in Week 9 with him and Quenton Nelson (knee) both set to be sidelined against the Cardinals.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Velus Jones Jr. (hamstring) set to play Sunday
items.desc: Velus Jones Jr. (hamstring) is set to play in Sunday's game against the Arizona Cardinals.
items.impact: Jones has been managing a nagging hamstring issue recently, but he is set to be available to play on Sunday. Fantasy managers shouldn't expect him to be relevant for the foreseeable future, however.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Rashid Shaheed (knee) won't play Sunday
items.desc: Rashid Shaheed (knee) won't play in Sunday's game against the Arizona Cardinals.
items.impact: The veteran is going to be sidelined again on Sunday as he continues to battle a knee issue of some kind. Tory Horton may see more work as a result of his absence, but that isn't likely to matter much with Drew Lock set to start at quarterback in the absence of Sam Darnold (quad/ribs) this week.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Talanoa Hufanga (ankle) listed questionable for Sunday
items.desc: Talanoa Hufanga (ankle) is listed questionable for Sunday's game against the Carolina Panthers.
items.impact: Hufanga missed last week's game due to an ankle injury that he's dealing with, but he is questionable and will have a chance to make his return to the lineup on Sunday. Denver's secondary will be significantly stronger if he's available to suit up and play for them in this game.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Brandon Jones (hamstring) sidelined for Sunday
items.desc: Brandon Jones (hamstring) will be sidelined for Sunday's game against the Carolina Panthers.
items.impact: Jones suffered a hamstring injury in last week's game and won't be available to play on Sunday as a result. Denver's secondary will be weaker with him out of the lineup against Carolina.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Pat Bryant (ankle) questionable to play Sunday
items.desc: Pat Bryant (ankle) is questionable to play in Sunday's game against the Carolina Panthers.
items.impact: Bryant has missed several weeks while on injured reserve, but he was able to practice in full all week and is now considered questionable to make his return on Sunday. He isn't likely to be a strong fantasy option for his first game or two back even if active, but his presence should help QB Bo Nix and Denver's offense as a whole.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Jaelan Phillips (hamstring) remains out for Sunday
items.desc: Jaelan Phillips (hamstring) remains out for Sunday's game against the Denver Broncos.
items.impact: Phillips is set to be sidelined for a third-straight game on Sunday as he continues to nurse a hamstring issue of some kind. Carolina's defensive front will be weaker with him unavailable to play in this matchup against the Broncos.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Bobby Okereke (foot) sidelined for Sunday
items.desc: Bobby Okereke (foot) will be sidelined for Sunday's game against the Denver Broncos.
items.impact: The veteran linebacker will be sidelined on Sunday due to a foot issue that he's managing. His absence will be less than ideal for the Panthers ahead of a matchup against the Broncos.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Damien Lewis (knee) unavailable for Sunday
items.desc: Damien Lewis (knee) will be unavailable for Sunday's game against the Denver Broncos.
items.impact: Lewis is set to be sidelined again on Sunday. He's still managing a knee issue and will need more time off in order to make a full recovery. Carolina's offensive line is dealing with several injuries right now and will likely struggle a bit against a tough Denver defensive front this week.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Mason Taylor (back) without injury designation for Sunday
items.desc: Mason Taylor (back) is without an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Kansas City Chiefs.
items.impact: Taylor was limited at practice earlier in the week due to a back injury, but he's now off of the injury report and good to go for Week 9. He isn't expected to be a consistent fantasy contributor for the foreseeable future, however.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: David Bailey (groin) will play Sunday
items.desc: David Bailey (groin) will play in Sunday's game against the Kansas City Chiefs.
items.impact: Bailey will be available to play on Sunday. He has been dealing with a groin injury for a little while, but he seems to be back to about full health now. His return is good news for New York's defensive front.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Breece Hall (quad) off injury report for Sunday
items.desc: Breece Hall (quad) is off of the injury report for Sunday's game against the Kansas City Chiefs.
items.impact: Hall is now off of the injury report entirely heading into the weekend, meaning that he is fully good to go and will make his return to the lineup on Sunday. He still has explosive week-to-week potential, but he may be more inconsistent moving forward now that Braelon Allen has earned more touches for himself while serving as the team's temporary RB1.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Ronnie Rivers (calf) set to make return Sunday
items.desc: Ronnie Rivers (calf) is set to make his return in Sunday's game against the Washington Commanders.
items.impact: Rivers has been sidelined for most of the season while recovering from a calf issue of some kind, but he is healthy again and is set to make his return to the lineup on Sunday. He isn't expected to be fantasy relevant for the foreseeable future, however, being relegated to a depth role behind Kyren Williams and Blake Corum for the time being.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Kam Curl (foot) questionable for Sunday
items.desc: Kam Curl (foot) is questionable for Sunday's game against the Washington Commanders.
items.impact: Curl was able to return to practice in a limited fashion on Friday, but he may still miss Sunday's game due to the foot injury that he's managing right now. That would leave Los Angeles' secondary short-handed ahead of a favorable matchup against the Commanders.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Terrance Ferguson (ankle) without injury designation for Sunday
items.desc: Terrance Ferguson (ankle) is without an injury designation for Sunday's game against the Washington Commanders.
items.impact: Ferguson is going to be available to play on Sunday, despite being listed on the injury report earlier in the week due to an ankle issue. He may see more involvement than usual if Colby Parkinson (ribs) is ruled out for the Rams.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Myles Garrett (knee/rest) cleared to play Sunday
items.desc: Myles Garrett (knee/rest) has been cleared to play in Sunday's game against the Washington Commanders.
items.impact: Garrett has been sidelined since Week 1 due to a knee injury of some kind, but he is now healthy again and is set to make his return to the lineup on Sunday. His presence will offer a significant boost to Los Angeles' defensive front moving forward, even if it takes him a week or two to return to full form.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Steve Avila (hamstring) off injury report for Sunday
items.desc: Steve Avila (hamstring) is off of the injury report for Sunday's game against the Washington Commanders.
items.impact: A hamstring injury affected Avila's participation at practice early in the week, but it's not a serious issue and won't prevent him from playing on Sunday. His presence will continue to be important for Los Angeles' offense on a week-to-week basis moving forward.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Matthew Stafford (elbow) good to go for Sunday
items.desc: Matthew Stafford (elbow) is good to go for Sunday's game against the Washington Commanders.
items.impact: As expected, Stafford's elbow injury is nothing serious at this point and won't prevent him from playing on Sunday. He should be good to go, although he is harder to trust starting on a week-to-week basis now with several key pass catchers sidelined due to injury for the Rams.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Dyami Brown (calf) unavailable for Sunday
items.desc: Dyami Brown (calf) is unavailable for Sunday's game against the Los Angeles Rams.
items.impact: Brown recently suffered a calf injury and is going to be unavailable to play on Sunday because of it. The Commanders have also ruled out Treylon Burks (foot) for that matchup, so they will likely need to lean heavily on rookie Antonio Williams in Week 9.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Jer'Zhan Newton (pec) questionable for Sunday
items.desc: Jer'Zhan Newton (pec) is questionable for Sunday's game against the Los Angeles Rams.
items.impact: Newton may be available to make his season debut on Sunday after spending the start of the season recovering from a procedure he underwent on his pec. His return, whenever it comes, will be a nice boost for Washington's defensive front moving forward.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Treylon Burks (foot) won't play Sunday
items.desc: Treylon Burks (foot) won't play in Sunday's game against the Los Angeles Rams.
items.impact: The Commanders are going to be down a key wideout on Sunday, with Burks set to be sidelined due to a foot issue that he's dealing with. Dyami Brown (calf) is also set to be sidelined, so rookie Antonio Williams is expected to see a large portion of the team's targets this week.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Jacob Saylors (neck) listed questionable for Sunday
items.desc: Jacob Saylors (neck) is listed questionable for Sunday's game against the Miami Dolphins.
items.impact: Saylors is uncertain to play on Sunday due to the neck injury that he's currently recovering from. Sione Vaki (ankle) is also uncertain to play, so it looks like Detroit might not have much healthy depth behind Jahmyr Gibbs in the backfield this week.

items.author: Leo Sells
items.title: Sione Vaki (ankle) considered questionable for Sunday
items.desc: Sione Vaki (ankle) is considered questionable for Sunday's game against the Miami Dolphins.
items.impact: Vaki is uncertain to play on Sunday, as he's currently dealing with some kind of an ankle issue. Jacob Saylors (neck) is also questionable to play, so it's uncertain who will be available to play the RB2 role behind Jahmyr Gibbs for the Lions this week.
